title: Knowlify vs TubeScience: Which Ad Partner Fits Your Brief?
summary: Knowlify vs TubeScience compared on payment model, creative scope, Meta campaign management and scale, using each company's published terms as of October 2026.
body_markdown:
## How do the payment models differ?


Knowlify's public terms are a starting price of $5,000 a month and a conditional 90-day refund. TubeScience's public terms are a pay-for-performance fee whose rate, trigger and measurement period sit in the proposal. Those are different mechanisms. A refund changes the remedy when its conditions are met, while a performance fee changes how the bill is calculated.


Keep three columns in your comparison: production fees, media spend, and any refund or performance fee. Buyers often mix these together, and that makes two proposals look more alike than they are.


Ask TubeScience for a worked invoice built from its actual formula, covering three scenarios. The first is a normal month. The second is a month when you pause spend because stock runs out. The third is a month when a strong ad keeps running after the first production round. For each, ask what qualifies for payment, which period is measured, what is excluded and who makes the account decisions.


Do not assume a percentage. The public materials do not verify a fee rate, and a figure from a sales call should go into the written proposal before you rely on it. Bring that sample month to a[scoping call](https://knowlify.com/book) and check each line with the provider before you sign.


## Which scale and workload fit each option?


Count the ads your media team can test in a month, then compare providers against that number. Knowlify's stated cadence is about 25 finished ads a week, with creative-only work for a team that has its own buyer. Creatify Studio's page describes 25 to 100 or more videos a month. TubeScience's FAQ flags seven-figure monthly spend as the level where a team should be ready to scale.


Capacity is not quality. Ask each provider to produce the same batch for your brief, using the same review steps, and count the approval work that remains on your side. A large weekly volume helps only when your account can test it.


## What Meta and FTC rules apply to AI ads?


Meta's generative AI transparency update says it labels ads created or significantly edited with its own generative AI creative features. When those tools add a photorealistic AI-generated person, the label appears next to the Sponsored label. Meta also says it will detect ads made or edited with third-party AI tools and show an "AI info" label in About this ad, and the post does not say that detection is live yet.


Plan for the label in either model. The[Meta transparency update](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/02/gen-ai-transparency-metas-ads-products/) sets out the rules, and your proposal should say who handles any disclosure.


The FTC is more specific about content. Its[testimonial guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers) says there is no blanket ban on AI avatars in marketing, but an avatar is prohibited when the testimonial it delivers is fake or false. Its[advertising guidance](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/advertising-faqs-guide-small-business) says advertisers need evidence for their claims. A tool is not evidence that an ad's claims are true, so assign claim substantiation in the contract whichever model you choose.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick for finished AI video ads on Facebook and Instagram, with optional Meta campaign management, from $5,000 a month.
- TubeScience's performance fee has no published rate or formula, so ask for worked invoices before you compare it with a quote.
- Knowlify's 90-day guarantee is a conditional refund under written terms, which is a different remedy from a performance fee. Managed plans carry an agreed target in 30 days instead.
- If you need real people filmed, shortlist creator platforms, because Knowlify does not supply real human creators.
- Count the ads your account can test each month, and compare providers on that workload.


## FAQ


### What is the best alternative to TubeScience?


Our pick is Knowlify, a done-for-you AI video ads agency for Facebook and Instagram that makes about 25 finished ads a week and has a person check each one before delivery. Choose Valid if you want creative and media buying in one proposal, or Superside if video shares a queue with design. Compare every finalist on the same brief and the same payment terms.


### Is TubeScience pay for performance?


As of October 2026, TubeScience describes its offer that way on its public website. The public materials do not state the full contract formula. Ask for the payment trigger, the measurement method and worked billing examples.


### Does Knowlify offer performance-based pricing?


Knowlify's public pricing starts at $5,000 a month. Its guarantee is separate: if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days, you can cancel by email for a full refund. Managed plans carry an agreed target in 30 days instead. Read the terms on the site before you rely on it.


### Can Knowlify run my Meta campaigns too?


Yes, as an option. Knowlify can manage your Facebook and Instagram campaigns end to end, or deliver creative only for a team that already has a media buyer. It does not run TikTok, LinkedIn, Google or YouTube ads.


### How should I compare the two proposals fairly?


Give both providers the same brief, the same number of concepts and the same approval steps. Then compare the written fee, the performance formula, the refund conditions and the work that stays with your team. Keep media spend in its own column, and treat a proposal without a worked invoice as unpriced.
